MUNSAN, KOREA, JUNE 2 (AP)-A SINGLE ISSUE BLOCKS AN END TO THE COST- 
LY KOREAN CONFLICT--EXCHANGE OF WAR PRISONERS. | 

THIS ISSUE IS SO SIMPLE IT LEAVES WO MEETING GROUND FOR COMPROMISE. 
ONE SIDE MUST GIVE IN. 

THE ALLIES REFUSE TO EMPLOY FORCE TO SEND BACK NORTH KOREAN OR 
CHINESE SOLDIERS. A RECENT PRISONER POLL SHOWS NEARLY 100,000 OF THE 
169,000 FORMER FIGHTING MEN AND CIVILIANS NOW IN U.Ne STOCKADES 
WOULD RISK DEATH RATHER THAN RE-EMBRACE COMMUNISM. 

THE COMMUNISTS DEMAND ALL THEIR MEN COME HOME, REGARDLESS OF 
INDIVIDUAL WISHES. 

THIS CONTROVERSY HAS SPARKED THE FIERCEST DEBATES OF THE LONG=DRAWN 
OUT TRUCE CONFERENCES. 

FOR THREE WEEKS THE TALKS ACTUALLY HAVE WALLOWED IN FRUITLESS 
LANGUAGE SPATS«

TENT FOR WHAT THE ALLIES CALL THE MOST VICIOUS, DEGRADING PROPAGANDA 
HEARD SINCE THE TRUCE TALKS STARTED LAST JULY.

"SLAUGHTER HOUSES." AND HE ASSERTS THE ALLIES ARE HOLDING HIS SOLDIERS 
TO REARM THEM FOR "CANNON-FODDER."

THE CONFERENCE TENT.

MACKINAC. ISLAND, MICH. JUNE 2 (AP)-A NUCLEAR PHYSICIST WHO 
HELPED CREATE THE ATOM BOMB APOLOGIZED FOR THE HIROSHIMA AND NAGASAKI 
BOMBINGS TO A JAPANESE DELEGATION AT THE WORLD ASSEMBLY OF MORAL 
RE-ABMAMENT (MRA) TODAY. 

ReJe MOON, UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO PROFESSOR, ADDRESSED HIS APOLOGY 
DIRECTLY TO tuo FORMER JAPANESE CABINET MINISTERS WHO SHARED THE 
SPEAKER'S PLATFORM WITH HIM. 

THE SCIENTIST SAID HE WAS SORRY THAT THE TREMENDOUS ENERGY OF 
NUCLEAR FISSION HAD BEEN USED TO DESTROY RATHER THAN TO PROVIDE 
BENEFITS FOR MANKIND. 

HIS APOLOGY WAS ACCEPTED BY KEIZO SHIBUSAWA, FORMER MINISTER OF 
FINANCE AND HEAD OF THE JAPANESE DELEGATION TO THE ASSEMBLY. 

SHIBUSAWA STEPPED FOWARD AND SHOOK HANDS WITH PROF. MOONe HE 
PROMISED TO SPREAD THE IDEOLOGY OF MRA TO HIS FRIENDS IN JAPAN. 
FOLLOWERS OF THE MOVEMENT, WHICH IS COMBATTING COMMUNISM, BELIEVE 
THE WORLD'S PROBLEMS CAN BE SOLVED BY ITS PHILOSOPHY OF ABSOLUTE 
HONESTY, PURITY. UNSELFISHNESS AND LOVE. 

THE APoLocy ALso WAS ACCEPTED BY KANJU KATO, FORMER MINISTER OF 
LABOR AND A MEMBER OF THE RIGHT WING SOCIALIST PARTY. 

"JAPAN LOST THE WAR," KATO SAID. "BUT WE GAINED A NEW POLITICAL 
ime Por ,WE NEED TO FOSTER THE IDEAS OF DEMOCRACY WE HAVE 

PROF. MOON CALLED THE ATOM BOMB A FRANKENSTEIN==-SOMETHING THAT 
DESTROYS ITS CREATOR. 

THE SCIENTIST DECLARED, "ONLY THOSE PEOPLE WHO ALLOW THE HOLY 
SPIRIT TO DWELL IN THEM AND LIVE ABSOLUTE MORAL LIVES CAN 
UTILIZE NUCLEAR FUEL AS A BLESSING TO MANKIND SO THAT WE CAN ENJOY 
THE BENEFITS OF THE NUCLEAR AGE." 

IN ANOTHER ADDRESS, AAGE SCHULTZ, A MEMBER OF A DANISH STEEL WORKERS® 
UNION, TOLD THE ASSEMBLY WHY HE LEFT THE COMMUNIST PARTY AFTER j 
TWENTY YEARS TO FIGHT FOR MORAL RE-ARMAMENTe

MET_MRA,” HE SAID, “I'M NOT ANTI-COMMUNIST. THAT IS TOO CHEAP. TO 
WIN7A COMMUNIST YOu MUST SHOW HIM BIGGER IDEAS. IF YOU DO, YOU CAN BE

WASHINGTON. JUNE 3-CAP)=SENs. YOUNG (R-ND) SAID TODAY ADDED RESTRIC- 
BE PLACED ON IMPORTE&lt;OF OATS. BARLEY, RYE AND FEED WHEAT 
IN ORDER TO GIVE AMERICAN PRODUCERS A FAIR PRICE. 

NE AND SEN. MUNDT (R-SD) HAVE JOINED YESTERDAY IN OFFERING AN AMEND- 
MENT TO LEGISLATION EXTENDING THE PRESENT DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT BEYOND 
JUNE 3O.WHICH WOULD: 

. CONPYNUE THE PRESENT BAN ON IMPORTS OF BUTTER AND OTHER FATS 
AND OILS AND RESTRICT IMPORTS ON CHEESE. 

2. ADD OATS. BARLEY. RYE AND FEED WHEAT TO A RESTRICTED LIST SO THE 
SECRETARY OF AGRICULTURE COULD REDUCE IMPORTS OF THESE GRAINS IF THEY 
WERE INJURING AMERICAN PRODUCERS. 

YOUNG SAID IN A PREPARED SENATE SPEECH THAT IMPORTS OF THESE GRAINS 
FROM CANADA WERE NOT ONLY FORCING FARMERS IN THIS COUNTRY SHARPLY TO 
REDUCE THEIR ACREACE ON THESE GRAINS BUT WERE COSTING THE GOVERNMENT A 
LARGE AMOUNT IN ITS SUPPORT PROGRAM. 

MEANWHILE. YOUNG ASKED SECRETARY OF AGRICULTURE BRANNAN FOR A 
THOROUGH INVESTIGATION OF THE ACTIVITIES OF CARGILL, INCe, IN THE OATS 
FUTURES MARKET. 

IN A LETTER TO BRANNAN, YOUNG SAID IT APPEARED THAT CARGILL, INC. 
HAS BEEN THE PRINCIPAL IMPORTER OF CANADIAN OATSe HE ASKED THAT JM 
UEHL ADMINISTRATOR OF THE COMMODITY EXCHANGE AUTHORITY, INSTITUTE AN 
NVESTIGATION. 

STRESSING AGAIN THE EFFECT OF CANADIAN IMPORTS, HE’WROTEs "I AM 
CERTAIN THAT THE CONGRESS NEVER CONTEMPLATED THAT THE PRICE SUPPORT 
PROGRAM WOULD BE USED. IN EFFECT, TO BOLSTER PRICES TO CANADIAN PRO- 
DUCERS. BUT THIS HAS BEEN HAPPENING FOR YEARS X X xX." 

YOUNG TOLD THE SENATE THAT IN THE 1930S AMERICAN FARMERS HARVESTED 
AN AVERAGE OF ABOUT 3 1/2 MILLION ACRES OF RYE A YEAR. THIS COMPARES 
WITH AN ESTIMATE FOR THIS YEAR OF 1,381,000 ACRES. : 

"WHY HAS RYE PRODUCTION FALLEN OFF?" YOUNG ASKED. "THE ANSWER IS 
THAT IMPORTS, PRIMARILY FROM CANADA, HAVE NCREASED SUBSTANTIALLY.® 

OUNG SAID THE IMPORTS "EFFECTIVELY DETERMINE THE PRICE OF RYE FOR 
OUR DOMESTIC PRODUCERS." _ 

A PREVIOUS DUTY OF 15 CENTS A BUSHEL ON RYE IMPORTS HAS BEEN REDUCED 

BY STATE DEPARTMENT NEGOTIATIONS TO ONLY SIX CENTS A BUSHEL NOW, THE 


SENATOR SAID, WHILE THAT FOR OATS HAS BEEN CUT FROM 16 TO FOUR CENTS. 
B2swx 


"IN THE CASE OF OATS, IMPORTS FROM CANADA WILL RUN A MINIMUM OF | 
50 MILLION SUSHELS AND PERHAPS MAY REACH 60 MILLION BUSHELS THIS YEAR, 

YOUNG SAID THE PRICE OF OATS IN NORTH DAKOTA ON MAY 15 HIT 59 CENTS 
A BUSHEL ON THE 1951 CROP WHILE THE SUPPORT PRICE WAS 65 CENTS A BUSHEL 
THE SUPPORT LEVEL HAS BEEN RAISED TO 70 CENTS A BUSHEL FOR THE 1952 


~ YOUNG SAID IT WAS EXPENSIVE FOR THE GOVERNMENT TO SUPPORT THE PRICE 
OF OATS UNDER SUCH CIRCUMSTANCES« ,

ISLAND KOREA, THURSDAY, JUNE 5-(AP)-AMERICAN INFANTRYMEN 
SUPPORTED BY TANKS MARCHED INTO’A COMPOUND OF 3,340 COMMUNIST CIVILIAN 
PRISONERS TODAY AND THREW UP A DOUBLE BARBED WIRE FENCE CUTTING THE 
ENCLOSURE IN HALF. 

THERE WAS NO RESISTANCE. 

THE MANEUVER WAS THE FIRST MOVE IN BRIG. GEN. HAYDON Le. (BULL) 
BOATNER'S PLAN TO BREAK UP THE 17 BIG COMPOUNDS HOLDING AS MANY AS {, 
6,000 PRISONERS EACH INTO UNITS OF 500 EACH. | 


BOATNER HIMSELF WENT INTO THE COMPOUND ABOUT ONE HOUR AFTER HIS | 
TROOPS ENTERED. HE REMAINED INSIDE FOR A SHORT TIME. | 
IT WAS BELIEVED TO BE THE FIRST TIME THE TOUGH NEW COMMANDER OF THE 
KOJE STOCKADE HAD ENTERED A PRISON COMPOUND. NORTH KOREAN PRISONERS 
LAST MONTH SEIZED AN AMERICAN GENERAL IN COMMAND OF THE CAMP AND HELD 
HIM CAPTIVE FOR FOUR DAYS. | 
~ BOATNER*S BATTLE-TESTED SOLDIERS YESTERDAY DRAGGED DOWN THE LAST | 
COMMUNIST FLAGS AND DEFIANT SIGNS FROM THE UNRULY COMPOUNDS ON THIS | 
TIMPESTUOUS ALLIED ISLAND STOCKADE HOLDING SOME 80,000 RED PRISONERS. | 
THREE PATTON TANKS RUMBLED INTO COMPOUND 607 TODAY AHEAD OF ONE 
COMPANY OF SOLDIERS WEARING GAS MASKS AND CARRYING FIXED BAYONETS. 
A SECOND COOMPANY FOLLOWED WITH TOOLS AND ERECTED THE FENCE ACROSS 
THE CENTER OF THE COMPOUND. 


BOATNER DISCLOSED TODAY THAT FOOD HAD BEEN WITHHELD FROM THREE 
COMPOUNDS ON SEPARATE DAYS THIS WEEK AS AN ADMINISTRATIVE MEASURE. 
HE SAID THE ACTION WAS TAKEN IN STRICT CONFORMITY WITH THE 
GENEVA CONVENTION ON THE TREATMENT OF PRISONERS OF WAR. 
THE ACTION WAS NOT DISCIPLINARY, BOATNER SAID. 
"AT NO. TIME HAVE WE WITHHELD RATIONS AS A WEAPON TO OBTAIN 
OBEDIENCE TO ANY ORDER, NOR HAVE WE EVER THREATENED TO DO SO," HE SAID 
A STATEMENT FROM BOATNER'S HEADQUARTERS SAID IN PARTS 
“RATIONS WERE NOT ISSUED TO COMPOUNDS 96 AND 85 ON 4 JUNE. IT 
WAS KNOWN WE WOULD ENTER THOSE COMPOUNDS WITH A BATTALION OF 
INFANTRY AND SOME TANKS DURING THE DAY BECAUSE OF DEFIANCE OF 
ORDERS. NO RATIONS WE ISSUED THAT DAY AS AN ADMINISTRATIVE MATTER

NINE LEADING NON-COMMUNIST WORKERS’ DELEGATES SUBMITTED A 
RESOLUTION URGING GOVERNMENTS TO PERMIT TRADE UNIONS TO ESTABLISH RE- 
LATIONS WITH POLITICAL PARTIES, PROVIDED THAT SUCH RELATIONS DID NOT 
INTERFERE WITH THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC FUNCTIONS OF THE UNIONS. 

SIGNERS OF THE RESOLUTION, WHICH WILL BE CONSIDERED BY THE 
CONFERENCE DURING ITS THREE-GEEKS’ SESSION, INCLUDED GEORGE P. 
DELANEY OF THE UNITED STATES, ALFRED ROBERTS OF BRITAIN, LEON JOUHAUX 
OF FRANCE AND CLAUDE JODOIN OF CANAEA. | 

THE RESOLUTION DECLARED THAT THE FREEDOM OF LABOR UNIONS REQUIRED 
THAT THEY SHOULD BE ESTABLISHED "WITHOUT REGARD TO THE RACE 


NATIONAL ORGIN OR Pi ICAL AFFILIATION” OF THEIR MEMBERS, Anp THAT | 


THEY SHOULD BE FREE TO ESTABLISH RELATIONS WITH POLITICAL PARTIES AN) 
UNDERTAKE CONSTITUTIONAL POLITICAL ACTION, PROVIDED THAT "THE 
CONTINUANCE OF THE TRADE UNION MOVEMENT ok ITS SOCIAL AND_ ECONOMIC 
FUNCTIONS" WERE NOT COMPROMISED. 3

JUNE REMILITARIZATION OF EAST GERMANY HAS 
PROVOKED A RECORD FLIGHT OF REFUGEES TO WEST BERLIN, ESPECIALLY YOUTHS 
FLEEING CONSCRIPTION, WEST SECTOR AUTHORITIES SAID TODAY. 

ON TUESDAY 700 EAST GERMANS REGISTERED HERE AS REFUGEES. THIS WAS 
MORE THAN TRIPLE THE DAILY AVERAGE OF 180 TO 200 WHICH PREVAILED IN 
RECENT WEEKS, BEFORE THE COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED ITS 
REARMAMENT PLANS AND STARTED SEALING OFF EAST GERMANY FROM THE WEST. 

THE BIGGEST INCREASE WAS AMONG YOUNG MEN IN THE 18 TO 22 YEARS 
BRACKET WHO FEARED BEING DRAFTED INTO THE “PEOPLE*S POLICE" ARMY.

WASHINGTON, JUNE 4=(AP)-HOUSE INVESTIGATORS SEARCHING FOR THE TRUTH 
ABON MASSACRE WERE TOLD AGALN TODAY THAT IT WAS THE RUSSIANS 
--AND NOT THE GERMANS--¥HO DID THE HTERING. 

FOUR THOUSAND POLISH OFFICERS WERE MURDERED IN KATYN FOREST, INSIDE 
RUSSIA, EARLY IN 1940. THE COMMUNISTS BLAMED THE NAZIS FOR THE MAS= 
SACRE, AND THE NAZIS BLAMED THE COMOINISTS. 

BORIS OLSHANSKY, A FORMER RED ARMY MAJOR WHO APPEARED VOLUNTARILY 
BEFORE THE SPECIAL INVESTIGATING COMMITTEE, SAID THE RUSSIANS DEFINITE- 
LY WERE TO BLAMEe HE TOLD THIS STORY TO SUPPORT HIS CONCLUSIONS | 

IN 1946 HE HAD A CONVERSATION WITH LTeGENeNeNeBURDENKO, NOW DEAD 
WHO TOLD HIM PRIVATELY THAT “OUR NKVD (SECRET POLICE) FRIENDS MADE A 
MISTAKE" IN MURDERING THE OLISH OFFICERS, WHO WERE PRISONERS OF WAR. 

BURDENKO, ONCE CHIEF SURGEON OF THE RED ARMY, HEADED A SPECIAL SOVIET 
MISSION WHICH IN 1944 ISSUED A REPORT ON THE MASSACRE. THIS REPORT i) 
UNLIKE THE PRIVATE REMARKS ATTRIBUTED TO HIM BY TODAY'S WITNESS, PLACED 
THE RESPONSIBILITY ON THE GERMANS. 

OLSHANSKY TESTIFIED THAT FROM THE BEGINNING HE DIDN'T HAVE ANY DOUBT 
THAT IT WAS “ONE OF THE SOVIE TRICKS." 

BURDENKO, HE SAID, WOULD HAVE LOST_HIS HEAD IF HE HAD NOT SIGNED 
THE MISSION'’S REPORT. 

OTHER WITNESSES ALSO HAVE ACCUSED THE RUSSIANS OF THE MASS MURDER. 
THE RUSSIAN GOVERNMENT, STILL STANDING ON THE BURDENKO REPORT, HAS REFUS 
ED TWO INVITATIONS TO PRESENT EVIDENCE TO THE INVESTIGATORS.

NEWWDELHI, INDIA, JUNE 5=(AP)-INDIA'S 14-MEMBER CULTURAL MISSION 
TO RED-CHINA, HEADED BY MRS. VIJAYALAKSHMI PANDIT, LEFT CANTON TODAY 
EXPECTING TO RETURN TO NEW DELHI TOMORROW AFTER-A FIVE-WEEK TOUR. 

PRIME MINISTER NEHRU'S CHOICES FOR THE MISSION DID NOT MAKE MUCH 
OF A HIT WITH LOCAL SYMPATHIZERS WITH COMMUNISM. OFFICIALS PRIVATELY 
HOPE THE MISSION WILL COME BACK WITH VIEWS SERVING TO BALANCE THE 
LOUD PRAISE OF THE COMMUNIST REGIME BY KeMe PANIKKAR, RETIRING INDIAN 
AMBASSADOR IN PEIPING. 

BESIDES MRS. PANDIT, THE SISTER OF NEHRU AND FORMER AMBASSADOR 
TO MOSCOW AND WASHINGTON, THE MISSION INCLUDED FRANK MORAES 
EDITOR OF THE INFLUENTIAL TIMES OF INDIA IN NEW DELHI AND BOMBAY, 
CHALAPATHI RAU, PRESIDENT OF THE INDIAN FEDERATION OF WORKING 
JOURNALISTS AND EDITOR OF THE LUCKNOW NATIONAL HERALD, AMARNATH JHA, 
FORMERLY VICE CHANCELLOR OF THREE UNIVERSITIES, AND SEVERAL POETS, 
PROFESSORS, ARCHITECTS, ARTISTS AND SOCIAL WORKERS. 

BEFORE LEAVING CANTON TODAY MRS. PANDIT SAID SHE HOPED THE 
"EXISTING FRIENDSHIP BETWEEN CHINA AND INDIA WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP 

N EVER“WIDENING AREAS OF MUTUAL UNDERSTANDING AND COOPERATION AND 


COME A POWERFUL FACTOR IN PROMOTION OF WORLD PEACE."

THE NETHERLANDS .JUNE S-(AP)-IRAN'S OLD AND AILING PREMIER 
MOHAM GOFS BEFORE THE INTERNATIONAL.COURT OF JUSTICE 
TOMORROW TO ITS JUDCES THEY ARE NOT COMPETENT TO RULE ON THE 
ANGLO-IRANIAN OIL DISPUTE. 

FOR“TRE-FIRST TIME IN THE U.N. -SPONSORED TRIBUNAL'S POSTWAR HISTORY 
THE HEAD OF A STATE APPEARS IN PERSON TO PLEAD HIS COUNTRY’S CASE. 
ADVANCE NOTICE OF HIS EMOTIONAL AND OFTEN TEARFUL ADDRESSES IN PUBLIC 
HAS CREATED SO MUCH INTEREST THAT 100 ADDITIONAL SEATS HAVE BEEN 
PROVIDED IN THE BIG HALL OF THE PEACE PALACE. 

MOSSADEGH, DESCRIBED BY HIS SON AND PHYSICIAN DR.G.H.MOSSADEGH AS 
"SICKER THAN’ EVER." HAS BEEN HERE SINCE MAY 27 PREPARING THE STATEMENT 
HE WILL MAKE TOMORROW. HIS "POLITICAL" SPEECH IS THE PREFACE TO A 
S4-PAGE STATEMENT IN WHICH HIS GOVERNMENT CLAIMS THAT NATIONALIZATION 
OF THE VAST BRITISH-OWNED ANGLO-IRANIAN OIL COMPANY INSTALLATIONS IN 
IRAN 15 MONTHS AGO IS AN INTERNAL MATTER. 

CONFRONTING MOSSADEGH WILL BE BRITAIN'S ATTORNEY GENERAL, SIR 
LIONEL HEALD AND HIS TOP ADVISERS, PRESSING THE BRITISH CLAIM THAT 
IRAN'S SEIZURE WAS A BREACH OF INTERNATIONAL LAW, MAKING THE WORLD 
COURT COMPETENT TO RULE ON WHETHER IRAN SHOULD PAY COMPENSATION AND 
DAMAGES. THE BRITISH GOVERNMENT OWNED 51 PER CENT OF THE SHARES 
IN THE BILLION ‘DOLLAR COMPANY. 

THE HEARING TOMORROW IS MERELY ON THE COURT'S COMPETENCE, AND THIS 
PRELIMINARY PHAZE OF THE CASE IS EXPECTED TO LAST MORE THAN TWO WEEKS. 
A DECISION IS NOT EXPECTED BEFORE THE END OF JULY. FOLLOWING 
MOSSADEGH*S OPENING ADDRESS, THE IRANIAN ARGUMENTS WILL BE HANDLED 
BY BELGIAN ATTORNEY HENRY ROLIN. 

THE BRITISH CASE RESTS ON THE CLAIM THAT A "NO-NATIONALIZATION" 
GUARANTEE WAS WRITTEN INTO THE ANGLO-IRANIAN AGREEMENT UNDER WHICH 
THE OIL COMPANY OPERATED ITS MULTI-MILLION=-DOLLAR REFINERY AND WELLS 
IN IRAN. 

BRITAIN ASKED THE WORLD COURT TO STEP INTO THE DISPUTE LAST MAY, 
AFTER NEGOTIATIONS AT THE IRANIAN CAPITAL OF TEHRAN BROKE DOWN. 

IRAN THEN -~ AS NOW -- SAID THE COURT HAD NO BUSINESS IN THE AFFAIR 
AND REFUSED TO SEND ANYONE TO ARGUE THE CASE. 

THE COURT DID NOT RULE ON THE CASE, BUT SUGGESTED THAT THE TWO 
COUNTRIES SET UP A JOINT INTERNATIONAL BOARD TO RUN THE OIL COMPANY. 
IRAN REJECTED THAT SUGGESTION, TOO. THERE IS NO MACHINERY BY WHICH 
THE COURT COULD FORCE A COUNTRY TO ABIDE BY ITS RULING. 

DESPITE HIS 76 YEARS AND THE FACT THAT HE OFTEN RUNS HIS NATION'S 
AFFAIRS FROM A SICKBED. MOSSANFGH HAS RFFEN UNTIRING AND UNRELENTING

THESE SUCCESSES BY THE NATIONALISTIC MOSSADEGH AT HOME AND ABROAD

AND WITH THE NATION FACING A GROWING ECONOMIC CRISIS FOR LACK OF THESE 
REVENUES --NEARLY 45 MILLION DOLLARS A YEAR.

REFINERY. LIVING COSTS HAVE RISEN AND THERE IS MOUNTING DISCONTENT 
WHICH CAN BE OF BENEFIT TO NO ONE BUT IRAN'S POWERFUL RED-RULED 
NEIGHBOR TO THE NORTH == RUSSIA.

BY WILLIAM JORDEN 

PUSAN, KOREA, TUESDAY, JUNE 10-CAP)-PRESIDENT SYNGMAN RHEE WAS 
EXPECTED TO REVEAL TODAY HIS REACTIONS TO A UNITED NATIONS PLAN 
FOR RELAXING POLITICAL TENSION IN SOUTH KOREA. 

UeN. AUTHORITIES HERE PROPOSED SUNDAY THAT THE PRESIDENT AND THE 
NATIONAL ASSEMBLY CALL OFF THEIR FEUD FOR AT LEAST 10 DAYS. THE AIM 
WAS TO LAY THE GROUND WORK FOR A POSSIBLE COMPROMISE. 

INTIMATES OF RHEE WERE NOT TOO HOPEFUL THE 77-YEAR-OLD PRESIDENT 
WOULD ADOPT THE U.N. PROPOSAL. THEY CITED HIS OPPOSITION TO INTER= 
FERENCE, HOWEVER WELL INTENTIONED, IN KOREA'S INTERNAL PROBLEMS. 

RHEE, FACING ALMOST CERTAIN DEFEAT FOR RE-ELECTION TO THE 
PRES IDENCY BY THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, IS INSISIHAT THE KOREAN 


PRESIDENCY BY THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, IS INSISTING THAT THE KOREAN 
PEOPLE BE ALLOWED TO PICK THE PRESIBENT DIRECTLY. A CONSTITUTIONAL | 
AMENDMENT TO THAT EFFECT WAS DEFEATED BY THE ASSEMBLY EARLY THIS YEAR, 

RHEE HAS SAID THE LEGISLATURE'S ACTION VIOLATES THE "WILL OF THE 
PEOPLE." TWO WEEKS AGO HE IMPOSED MARTIAL LAW AND PUT A DOZED 
OPPOSITION ASSEMBLYMEN IN JAIL. | 

ONE OF THEM IS ACCUSED OF MURDERING AN ARMY CAPTAIN LAST MONTH. THE 
OTHERS, HOWEVER, FACE CHARGES OF ACCEPTING BRIBES OR CONSPIRACY IN A 
*COMMURIST PLOT." |

THE COMPLAINT IN BOTH KIRGIZ AND GEORGIA WAS MOSTLY “BOURGEOIS 
NATIONALISM ,* WHICH MEANS THE PARTY LEADERSHIP FAILED TO PUT DOWN 
EFFECTIVELY THE REMNANTS OF NATIONALIST FEELING IN THE STATES. 
BOURGEOIS NATIONALISM MEANS RESPECT FOR ANY PHASE OF HISTORY OR 
CULTURE WHICH DOES NOT STEM DIRECTLY FROM MOSCOW AND GREAT RUSSIA. 
THE SOUTHEAST AREAS OF THE SOVIET UNION, PARTICULARLY GEORGIA AND THE 
TRANSCAUCASUS, LONG WERE HOTBEDS OF REBELLION AGAINST THE RUSSIAN 
CZARS.

BORDER WITH ASIA ARE THE TURKMEN, UZBEK AND TADZHIK REPUBLICS, WIIICH

CULATIONS AS PRODUCED THE KOREAN WAR AND WHICH, IF UNCERTAINTY CON- 
TINUES, COULD PRODUCE A FAR GREATER DISASTER."

ISLAND, MICHe, JUNE 10-(AP)=-MORAL RE-ARMAMENT*’S FOUNDER 
PLEADED TODAY FOR A FORCE TO BRING THE WORLD'S PEOPLES "TO THEIR 
SENSES BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE." 


THE PLEA CAME FROM 74=YEAR=OLD DR. FRANK Ne De BUCHMAN, THE ENGLISH= 
MAN WHO BEGAN THE MORAL RE“ARMAMENT MOVEMENT DEDICATED TO “ABSOLUTE 


MORAL STANDARDS. 
DRe BUCHMAN, DEPLORING WHAT HE CALLED A "BREAKDOWN OF CIVILIZATION," 
ONCLUDING SESSION OF THE ASSEMBLY, 


SPOKE TO THE C he 
THE ISLAND MEETING IN WHICH FOLLOWERS OF DRe BUCHMAN HAVE TESTI- 


S 
FIED TO MORAL REARMAMENT" S EFFECTS, HAVE BEEN ATTENDED BY 1,000 DELE- 


Mm GATES FROM 34 NATIONS. 
: GOVERNMENT LEADERS, MEN OF INDUSTRY AND LABOR, AND OTHERS HAVE 

JOINED IN ESPOUSING THE MOVEMENT'S PRINCIPLES OF "ABSOLUTE HONESTY, 
PURITY, UNSELFISHNESS AND LOVE." 

IN AIS TALK DR. BUCHMAN DEPLORED PRESENT WORLD CONDITIONS. ; 

"WE ARE IN THE MIDST OF THE BREAKDOWN OF OUR CIVILIZATION--WAR IN THE 
HOME, WAR IN INDUSTRY, WAR BETWEEN THE NATIONS." HE SAID» 

WHAT IS THE FUTURE?" HE ASKED. "FURTHER DISINTEGRATION CHAOS 
ANARCHY, AND DICTATORSHIP? OR THE BIRTH OF A NEW SOCIETY BROUCHT 
BY A REVOLUTIONARY CHANGE IN HUMAN NATURE?" 

HE WAS CRITICAL OF PEOPLE'S ATTITUDES. _ 

"SENDING OUR BOYS OUT TO DIE WHILE WE BLAME EVERYBODY BUT | 
OVERSELVES AND CONTINUE TO LIVE AS USUAL, SELFISHLY PADDING OURSELVES 
AGAINST REALITY, ONLY EMBITTERS AND CONFUSES." HE SAID« 

AMONG YESTERDAY'S NUMEROUS SPEAKERS AT THE ASSEMBLY WERE EUGENIE 
EBOUE, WIDOW OF THE GOVERNOR GENERAL OF EQUATORIAL AFRICA, AND DRe 
ERNEST CLAXTON OF LONDON, OFFICIAL OF THE BRITISH MEDICAL’ ASSOCIATION. 

MADAME EBOUE SAID THAT MORAL RE-ARMAMENT HAD TAUGHT HER TO GIVE - 
UP HER RESENTMENT AGAINST THE GERMANS THOUGH SHE HAD CONSIDERED THEM 
RESPONSIBLE FOR HER HUSBAND'S DEATH AFTER THE FALL OF FRANCE IN THE 

DRe CLAXTON CALLED ON HIS PROFESSION TO "ANSWER THE HEARTACHES OF 
PEOPLE AS WELL AS THE HEART DISEASES." HE SAID DOCTORS, IN ADDITION 
TO CURING MEN'S PHYSICAL ILLS, MUST BRING THEM “AN IDEA’TO LIVE BY AND 
A HOPE AND FAITH TO LIVE FOR. |

IN THIS GRIM MANEUVERING FOR BETTER TACTICAL POSITIONS IN THE EVENT 
OF A CHINESE OFFENSIVE, THE ALLIES CALLED IN THE AIR FORCE FROM ITS 
MAJOR TASK OF SMASHING COMMUNIST SUPPLY LINES AND BASES. 

WAVES OF FIGHTER=BOMBERS ROARED OVER THE HILLS, RAINING BOMBS, 
BULLETS AND FLAMING JELLIED GASOLINE ON THE CHINESE FROM DAWN TO DUSK. 

ALLIED PILOTS STILL FOUND TIME TO STAGE A HEAVY RAID ON A RED SUPPLY 
BASE ON THE NEARBY HAEJU PENINSULA. PILOTS REPORTED THEY DESTROYED

muti HEADQUARTERS MADE NO ESTIMATE OF THE NUMBER OF CHINESE

AN OFFICER SAID THE CHINESE WERE DUG IN ON THE WESTERN SLOPE AND 
ARTILLERY AND MORTAR FIRE WAS SEEKING THEM OUT. 

OME TANKS WHICH WADED INTO THE STRUGGLE IN SUPPORT OF THE INFANTRY 
RAN INTO COMMUNIST MINE FIELDS AND WERE DISABLED. 

THE CHINESE FIRED THEIR OWN ARTILLERY AND MORTARS AND BROUGHT 
UP SOME TANKS OR SELF=PROPELLED GUNS FOR DIRECT FIRE. 

ALLIED TANK AND INFANTRY TEAMS RAIDED OTHER CHINESE HILL POSITIONS 
ABOUT A MILE WEST OF THE CHORWON BATTLE. THEY REPORTED KILLING OR 
WOUNDING ABOUT 600 CHINESE IN CLOSE QUARTER FIGHTING,

SAIGON, INDOCHINA, JUNE 15-(AP)-KING NORODOM SIMANQMZ VARMEN OF | 
CAMBODTA FIRED THE NATIONALIST-BACYED GOVERNMENT OF THREE AUTONOMOUS 
MONARCHY IN THE FRENCH INDQCIINESE UNION TODAY AND SET MEMSELF UP AS 
PREMIERGOVER A MORE MODERA OVERNMENT OF PRINCES.* 
THE SO-YEAR-OLD WESTERN-MINDED RULER THUS BROUGHT TO A HEAD IIS 
FEUD WITH EXTREMISTS IN THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY GOVERNMENT OF PREMIER 


| UY KANTOU WHO NAVE BEEN PUSHING FOR IMMEDIATE AND COMPLETE 


INDEPENDENCE FROM THE FRENCII. 

HE ORDERED KANTOU AND HIS CABINET TO RESIGN AND SENT A MESSAGE TO 
THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY DEMANDING TIAT--UNDER THE THREAT OF DISSOLUTION== 
IT QUICKLY VOTE A SPECIAL LAW PLACING GOVERNMENTAL POWER IN HIS HANDS 
FOR THE NEXT THREE YEARS. 

KING NORODOM THEN ANNOUNCED THE FORMATION OF A NON-POLITICAL 
GOVERNMENT IN WHICH NEARLY ALL CABINET POSTS WERE FILLED BY PRINCES 
AND MEMBERS OF THE ROYAL ENTOURAGE, PRINCESS YYANTHOR, WHO REPRESENTS 
CAMBODIA AT THE FRENCH! UNION ASSEMBLY AT VERSAILLES, WAS NAMED 
MINISTER OF EDUCATION. 

IN A MESSAGE TO THE 3 1/2 MILLION PEOPLE OF THIS SOUTHERN INDOCHIN 
STATE, THE MONARCH ACCUSED THE OUSTED GOVERNMENT OF “COMPROMISING THE 
SITUATION ALMOST WITHOUT NOPE." ME PROMISED TO CLEAN UP TIE FINGDOM 
IN TWO YEARS AND TO BRING ABOUT GREATER INDEPENDENCE IN THREE. WIEN 
THIS MANDATE ENDED, HE SAID, HE WOULD BE READY TO FACE A POPULAR 
TRIBUNAL IN THE PRESENCE OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM SIX FOREIGN 
COUNTRIES TO ANSWER FOR HIS ACTIONS. 

AMBODIA, WITH ITS CAPITAL AT PNOMPENK, IS TIE SOUTHERNMOST OF THE 
THREE INDOCHINESE STATES MAVING UP THE FRENCH UNION. IT BORDERS oN 
THAILAND TO THE WEST. THE OTHER TWO STATES ARE THE TINY KINGDOM OF 
LAOS AND THE REPUBLIC OF VIET NAM--THE LARGEST--IHEADED BY FORMER 
EMPEROR BAO DAI. ALL THREE HAVE BEEN SEARED BY SIX YEARS OF WAR. 
AGAINST THE COMMUNIST=LED VIETMINII.

INTENDS TO FOLLOW A MORE REASONABLE POLICY ON THE GROUNDS THAT HIS 
TINY COUNTRY NEEDS THE SUPPORT OF THE FRENCH BOTH MILITARILY AND 
POLITICALLY. n ¢ IGH

“OREAN CIVILIAN INTERNEES TO MARCH OUT OF COMPOUND 62 FOR REDISTRIBUTION

vOJE'S BLOODIEST RIOT LAST FEB. 18 WHEN 85 REDS AND ONE AMERICAN

CIVILIAN COMMUNISTS.

SEARCH. THE RIFLES ARE BELIEVED TO BE BURIED OR TO HAVE BEEN TAKEN

BONN, GERMANY, JUNE 18-(AP)-THE FUTURE OF THE AMBITIOUS PLAN TO 
CREATE A EUROPEAN-ARMY TO WARD OFF 
POSSIBLE RUSSIAN AGGRESSION NOW RESTS WITH 24 GERMAN JURISTS. 

THESE JUDGES OF THE FEDERAL CONSTITUTION COURT IN THE SOUTH GERMAN 
CITY OF KARLSRUHE SOON MUST DECIDE WHETHER IT IS CONSTITUTIONAL FOR 
WEST GERMANY TO REARM AND JOIN THE EUROPEAN DEFENSE COMMUNITY (EDC). 

THE PLAN TO MERGE THE ARMED FORCES OF SIX NATIONS -- WEST GERMANY, 
FRANCE, ITALY, BELGIUM, HOLLAND AND LUXEMBOURG -- DOES NOT BEGIN 
TO WORK UNTIL’ALL SIX PARLIAMENTS HAVE RATIFIFD IT. 

IN WEST GERMANY THE OPPONENTS OF THE PLAN -- MOSTLY SOCIALISTS == 
ARE TRYING TO BLOCK RATIFICATION BY AN APPEAL TO THE CONSTITUTIONAL 
COURT, THEY CONTEND THAT THE CONSTITUTION, DRAWN UP THREE YEARS AGO 
WHEN GERMAN REARMAMENT WAS NOT CONTEMPLATED, MAKES NO PROVISION 
FOR THE RECRUITING OF ARMED FORCES. 

CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER'S GOVERNMENT REPLIES THAT NOTHING IN 
THE CONSTITUTION SPECIFICALLY FORBIDS MILITARY FORCES. 

WEST GERMANY'S PRESIDENT THEODOR HEUSS. WHO SIGNS ALL LAWS, ALSO 
HAS ASKED THE COURT TO SAY WHETHER THE PRESENT CONSTITUTION PERMITS 
WEST GERMANY TO REARM FOR HER DEFENSE, yr

WA JUNE 18-(AP)=PAUL GINSBERG, COMMANDER OF THE JEWISH WAR 
VETERANS. SAID TODAY HE IS CONVINCED THAT ANY FURTHER AGGRESSION BY 
COMMUNIST SATELLITES WILL LEAD THE FREE NATIONS TO CARRY THE FIGHT 


DIRECTLY TO RUSSIA. 

GINSBERG, OF ATLANTA,GA., TALKED WITH REPORTERS AFTER A VISIT WITH 
PRESIDENT TRUMAN AT THE’ WHITE HOUSE. HE HAS JUST RETURNED FROM A 
VISIT TO EUROPE AND THE FAR EAST, AND SAID HE REPORTED TO THE PRESIDENT 
ERS QUOTED THE PRESIDENT ONLY AS SAYING THE SITUATION IS 

BUT GINSBERG SAID HIS OWN CONVICTION, GAINED FROM CONFERENCES "WITH 
VIRTUALLY EVERY PRIME MINISTER, EVERY GENERAL AND EVERY LEADER OF THE 
FREE WORLD." IS THAT ANY FURTHER AGGRESSION BY A COMMUNIST SATELLITE 
WILL BE MET BY AN ATTACK ON THE RUSSIANS THEMSELVES. 

THE KREMLIN HAS BEEN TRYING TO CREATE A NUMBER OF INCIDENTS BY 
SATELLITE COUNTRIES IN AN EFFORT TO GET US INVOLVED AND TO SPEND OUR 
ENERGIES FIGHTING THESE SATELLITES,” HE SAID. 

"I PREDICT OUR MILITARY LEADERS KNOW THE SITUATION AND THAT ANY 
FURTHER AGGRESSION WILL NOT GET US INVOLVED WITH THE TENTACLES OF THE 
OCTOPUS, BUT WE WILL GO TO THE HEART OF THE OCTOPUS ITSELF." 

AT ANOTHER POINT, HE SAID$ 

"IF THERE IS ANY’NEW AGGRESSION BY COMMUNIST SATELLITES I AM 


CONVINCED THAT WE WILL CALL UPON RUSSIA TO STOP IT, AND IF IT DOES b 


NOT, WE WILL GO RIGHT TO WORK." 
AsvED ABOUT GINSBERG'S STATEMENTS, PRESIDENTIAL SECRETARY JOSEPH 
SHORT TOLD REPORTERS THAT GINSBERG "JUST EXPRESSED IIIS PERSONAL * / 5 
OPINION" AND "I HAVE NO COMMENT ON HIS PERSONAL OPINION.

ATOMIC DEFENSE 

(ADVANCE) WASHINGTON, JUNE 22-(AP)-AIR FORCE MAGAZINE SAID TODAY A PLAN 
CALLING FOR USE OF SMALL ATOMIC BOMBS AS AERIAL WEAPONS AGAINST AP- 
PROACHING ENEMY AIRCRAFT IS BEING CONSIDERED AT THE HIGHEST MILITARY 
“THE UNOFFICIAL BUT USUALLY WELL-INFORMED MAGAZINE IS PUBLISHED BY 
THE AIR FORCE ASSOCIATION, COMPOSED OF VETERANS AND PRESENT MEMBERS 
OF THE AIR FORCE. THERE WAS NO COMMENT IMMEDIATELY FROM THE 
DEFENSE DEPARTMENT. 

AIR FORCE MAGAZINE SAID THE PLAN WOULD APPLY NUCLEAR ENERGY °AS THE 
KEY TO A REVOLUTIONARY NEW AIR DEFENSE SYSTEM." IT SAID THE BOMBS 
WOULD BE DELIVERED EITHER BY PILOTLESS ATRCRAFT HAVING A RANGF OF 


SEVERAL HUNDRED MILES OR BY LARGE PATROL PLANES CARRYING ATOMIC AnTy- 
AIRCRAFT ROCKETS. 

“THE UTILIZATION OF THE ATOMIC BOMB FOR DEFENSIVE AS WELL AS OFFEN- 
SIVE PURPOSES, WIILE STILL A LONG, LONG WAY FROM ACTUALITY, IS THE 
FIRST RAY OF LIGHT TO BE FOUND IN AN OTHERWISE DARK PICTURE," IT ADDED 

THE MAGAZINE SAID THAT CURRENTLY THE UNITED STATES CAN COUNT ON THE" 
DESTRUCTION OF NO MORE THAN 5 PER CENT OF AN APPROACHING ENEMY BOMBER 
FORCE AT NIGHT OR IN BAD WEATHER. 

“SOME OF OUR BEST AUTHORITIES ON AIR DEFENSE NOW FEEL THAT, WITH 
ATOMIC DEFENSIVE WEAPONS, WE MAY BE ABLE TO KNOCK DOWN 95 PER’CENT 
UNDER ANY CONDITIONS ,* IT SAID. 

*THESE MEN DO NOt CLAIM THAT THE NATION WOULD BE SPARED WIDE- 
SCALE DESTRUCTION AND A HEAVY LOSS OF BLOOD AND TREASURE, 

“BUT THEY DO ANTICIPATE THAT IT WOULD HAVE A CHANCE, A VERY Goop 
CHANCE, OF SURVIVAL." 

THE MAGAZINE SAID THE PLAN IS MADE POSSIBLE THROUGH RECENT ADVANCES 
WHICH HAVE LED TO THE DESIGN OF SMALL BUT EFFICIENT A-BOMBS,

FREEDOM AWARDS GIVEN BY FREEDOM HOUSE. 

THEIR SELECTION FOR THE 1952 AWARDS WAS ANNOUNCED BY FORMER 
UNDER-SECRETARY OF STATE SUMNER WELLES, PRESIDENT OF FREEDOM HOUSE

SUPREME ALLIED COMMANDER IN EUROPE.

INSCRIBED: "SCIENTIST AND EDUCATOR WHOSE JUDGMENT AND 
COURAGE FAITHFULLY SERVE OUR DEMOCRACY."

TUMLIS , TUNISIA, JUNE 23=-(AP)-TUNISIAN NATIONALISTS REJECTED TODAY 
FRENCH OFFERS OF REFORMS IN THE PROTECTORATE'S ADMINISTRATION AND 


CALLED INSTEAD FOR AN INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE TO SETTLE THIS_NORTI 
AFRICAN DISPUTE. 

A NATIONALIST RESOLUTION, ADOPTED AT A MEETING THIS MORNING, CALLED 
FOR SETTLING TUNISIAN ISSUES "UNDER TERMS OF THE CHARTER OF THE 
UNITED NATIONS. ® 

TUNISIANS ARE DEMANDING A GREATER VOICE INTHEIR OWN INTERNAL AFFAIRS. 
THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT'S PROGRAM OF REFORMS SURVIVED A STORMY DEBATE 
DURING THE WEEKEND IN THE FRENCH NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, WHICH THREATENED 
TO UNSEAT FOREIGN MINISTER ROBERT SCHUMAN AS A RESULT OF HIS 
EFFORTS TO GRANT MORE HOME RULE TO TUNISIANS. 

RIGHT-WING FACTIONS CHARGED THE REFORMS SCHUMAN PROPOSED WENT TOO 
FAR: THE COMMUNIST BLOC AND SOCIALISTS OPPOSED THEM AS BEING TOO 
RESTRICTED. BECAUSE OF THIS SPLIT IN THE OPPOSITION, THE ASSEMBLY 
FAILED TO PASS A RESOLUTION CENSURING THE REFORM PROGRAM, LEAVING 
SCHUMAN FREE TO GO AHEAD WITH IT. 

SCHUMAN'S REFORMS, REJECTED TODAY BY THE POWERFUL NATIONALIST MOVE- 
MENT IN TUNISIA, WOULD GIVE MORE CABINET POSTS TO TUNISIANS, GIVE 
TUNISIANS PRIOR{TY IN CIVIL SERVICE JOBS, ESTABLISH A TWO-HOUSE 
PARLIAMENT -- ONE OF THEM ALL-TUNISIAN, THE OTHER HALF -TUNISTAN 
HALF FRENCI--AND WOULD PROVIDE FOR ELECTION OF MUNICIPAL COUNCILS. 

THE NATIONALIST MOVEMENT HAS INSISTED ON FULL INDEPENDENCE FOR THIS 
PROTECTORATE OF SOME 3,300,000 MOSLEMS, WHICH HAS BEEN UNDER FRENCH 
ADMINISTRATION SINCE 1231. NATIONALISTS HAVE BACKED UP THEIR INDE~ 
PENDENCE DEMANDS WITH VIOLENCE IN THE PAST SEVERAL MONTHS, AND POLICE 
REPORTS TODAY INDICATED THIS VIOLENCE MAY BE INTENSIFYING.

"WHY RATION AMMUNITION IN KOREA? TO THE AVERAGE READER, THE WORD

"IN DISTRIBUTING AMMUNITION FOR USE BY FIELD ARTILLERY UNITS 4 THERE 
MUST BE OBVIOUSLY SOME GAUGE, SOME TABLE BY WHICH DISTRIBUTION IS MADE. 
AS ITS GAUGE, THE ARMY USES TABLES, OR CHARTS, INDICATING THE AMOUNT 
OF AMMUNITION WICH A CERTAIN TYPE OF UNIT MAY BE EXPECTED TO FIRE, OR 
EXPEND, WITHIN A CERTAIN LENGTH OF TIME, UNDER GIVEN CONDITIONS. 

WWHEN THE VOREAN FICHTING STARTED, THESE TABLES WERE BASED ON WORLD 
WAR II EXPERIENCE. ALMOST IMMEDIATELY, HOWEVER, THE FAR EAST COMMAND 
REQUESTED AND OBTAINED APPROVAL FOR RATES OF FIRE WIIICH WERE SEVERAL 
TIMES GREATER THAN WORLD WAR II RATES. ALTHOUGH! THESE PROVED HIGHER 
THAN NECESSARY, AND HAVE NOW BEEN REVISED DOWNWARD, IN SEVERAL VERY 
IMPORTANT TYPES OF AMMUNITION THE RATE OF FIRE PER WEAPON PER DAY IN 
KOREA HAS REMAINED SUBSTANTIALLY ABOVE THE WORLD WAR II RATE. 

HIGHER AUTHORIZED RATES OF FIRE HAD TIE EFFECT OF DECREASING 
EXISTING SUPPLY IN TERMS OF DAYS THAT IT WOULD LAST, WHERE DEPOT 
STOCKS IN THE UNITED STATES WERE LOW, AND WHERE A CONSIDERABLE PORTION OFM 
THE EXISTING STOCKS REQUIRED TIME-CONSUMING RENOVATION BEFORE SHIPMENT, 7 
RHE LACK BAS SERTQUS. CONSEQUENTLY THESE TYPES OF AMMUNITION DID NOT 
REACH THE THEATRE TN SUFFICIENT VOLUME TO SUPPORT TRE AVTMORIZED RATE 

AND TO BUILD UP A REASONABLE OPERATING RESERVE. THUS, AMONG SOME TYPES 
OF AMMUNITION, IT WAS NECESSARY TO APPORTION THE AMOUNT AVAILABLE AL~

UNITED NATIONS, NeYe, JUNE 24-C(AP)-FRENCH DELEGATE JULES 
SUGGESTED TODAY A’ BAN ON BACTERIAL AND CHEMICAL WEAPONS SHOULD BE 
GIVEN HIGH PRIORITY IN A COMPROMISE DISARMAMENT SCHEME HE OUTLIN ERO 
TO THE DISARMAMENT COMMISSION. 

MOCH SAID AN INTERNATIONAL CONTROL BODY SHOULD BE GIVEN AUTHORITY 
TO PROHIBIT BACTERIAL AND CHEMICAL WEAPONS. HE SUGGESTED ATOMIC 
WEAPONS COULD BE PROHISITED LATER AND STOCKPILES OF ATOMIC BOMBS 
DESTROYED « 

THE FRENCH DELEGATE MADE HIS 45-MINUTE SPEECH TO THE DISARMAMENT 
COMMISSION DURING A DAY'S BREAK IN THE DEVELOPING FIGHT IN THE 
SECURITY COUNCIL BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND RUSSIA ON SOVIET 
CHARGES THAT THE UseSe AND UsN. ARE USING GERM WARFARE IN KOREA 
AND CHINAs THE COUNCIL WILL MEET TOMORROW AT 9330 AeMe (EeSeTe) 
WITH SOVIET DELEGATE JACO® AsMALIK EXPECTED TO CONTINUE HIS EFFORTS 
TO BLOCK ACTION ON AN AMERICAN DEMAND FOR AN INVESTIGATION OF THE 
KREMLIN CHARGES. 

HE UNITED STATES AND BRITAIN WITHHELD COMMENT ON MOCH'S IDEAS 
BUT MALIK CHIDED HIN FOR NOT PUTTING IN A CONCRETE PROPOSAL. 
MALIK SAID THE SUGGESTIONS WERE SO ABSTRACT THAT THEY APPEARED TO 
BE HEADED TOWARD OBSTRUCTION OX THE COMMISSION'S WORK. 

MOCH IS LEAVING LATER THIS WEEK FOR FRANCE TO JUMP INTO THE 
BATTLE AGAINST THE AGREEMENT WITH WEST GERMANY. PERSONS FAMILIAR 
WITH HIS VIEWS MERE SAID HIS SPEECH WAS AN ATTEMPT TO BRIDGE THE 
EAST-WEST GAP ON DISARMAMENT AND AN EFFORT TO TAKE BACK TO PARIS WITH 
HIM SOME SIGN OF AGREEMENT TO BE USED AS AMMUNITION AGAINST THE 
GERMAN PACT. 

MOCH SAID THE DISARMAMENT PLAN SHOULD CONTAIN THREE MAJOR STEPS 
INSTEAD OF A LONGER SCHEME PROPOSED BY THE UNITED STATES, WHICH THE 
AMERICANS HAVE SAID WOULD TAKE A MINIMUM OF TWO YEARS OR MAYBE LONGER. 

MOCH SUGGESTED THAT INTERNATIONAL CONTROL BE_UNDERTAKEN BY A 
SPECIAL BODY OR BY THE SECURITY COUNCIL. HE SAID HE FAVORED THE 
COUNCIL. AMERICANS HAVE OBJECTED TO THE VETO POWER IN THE COUNCIL 
AND HAVE INSISTED THERE MUST SE NO VETO IN THE CONTROL BODY. MOCH 
SAID DECISIONS WOULD HAVE TO BE UNANIMOUS ANYWAY. 

HERE, IN BRIEF, IS THE HEART OF UOCK'S PLAN: 

1. THE FIRST STAGE VOULD BE ONE OF DISCLOSURE AND VERIFICATION 
WHICH WOULD END IN A HALT ‘OF THE ARMAMENTS RACE AND A LIMITATION OF 
EFFECTIVE FORCES. THIS WOULD SHOW THE EXTENT OF THE WORLD'S ARMA-

QUALTTY OF “CONVENTIONAL WEAPO! ‘S$ PRODUCTION WOULD STOP ON ATOMIC

BERLIN, JUNE 26 (AP)-AN AMERICAN SOLDIER WAS SENTENCED TO FIVE 
YEARS HARD LABOR TODAY ON CHARGES THAT HE BROKE OUT OF A U,S, ARMY 
PRISON, AND DESERTED TO THE SOVIET ZONE OF GERMANY, 

THE U,S, ARMY COURT MARTIAL GAVE HIM LESS THAN THE MAXIMUM 13 
YEARS AND ONE MONTH BECAUSE HE ESCAPED FROM THE RUSSIANS AND 
BECAUSE OF KIS TESTIMONY THAT HE HAD BEEN BRUTALLY BEATEN, THROWN INTO 


| FORCED LABOR AND FORCED BY RUSSIAN THREATS TO SIGN ANTI-AMERICAN 


STATEMENTS , 

THE SENTENCE WAS HANDED TO PVT.RAY D.SCHULTZ, OF BATAVIA, N.Y., 
WHO WITH TWO SOLDIERS &lt;= PVT, CHARLES J.SCOTT OF DECATUR, ILL,, AND 
PVT,SIDNEY R,SPARKS OF TENNILLE, GA, == FLED FROM A WEST BERLIN ARMY 
STOCKADE LAST DEC,3 AND WENT TO THE RUSSIAN 20NE, SCHULTZ SPENT SIX 
MONTHS IN COMMUNIST HANDS BEFORE RETURNING EARLY THIS MONTH, THE 
OTHER TWO APPARENTLY STILL ARE IN THE EAST, 


THE THREE WERE IN THE STOCKADE AWAITING TRIAL ON CHARGES THEY 
ASSAULTED AND ROBBED A GERMAN TAXI DRIVER, 
IN REPLY TO AMERICAN INQUIRIES ABOUT SCHULTZ AND HIS COMPANIONS, 


THE RUSSIANS SAID IN AN OFFICIAL LETTER THAT THE THREE HAD ASKED FOR 
“POLITICAL ASYLUM TO WORK FOR PEACE,® 


SCHULTZ TOLD THE COURT HIS RUSSIAN CAPTORS KICKED HIM, GUN-WHIPPED 
MIM AND THREATENED HIM WITH EXILE TO SIBERIA IF ME DIDN'T SIGN 
THE STATEMENT, HE SAID ONE OF THE INJURIES HE RECEIVED IN THE BEATINGS 
BECAME INFECTED AND HE WAS SUBJECTED TO A POCKET~KNIFE OPERATION WITH- 


OUT ANESTHETIC, HE SHOWED UGLY SCAS ON HIS NECK TO PROVE IT, 

SCHULTZ TESTIFIED HE FINALLY MANAGED TO ESCAPE FROM A TEXTILE MILL 
AT BAUTZEN WHERE WE AND HIS BUDDIES HAD BEEN FORCED TO WORK, HE SAID 
HE ORIGINALLY HAD INTENDED TO STAY IN THE RUSSIAN SECTOR OF BERLIN 
OVERNIGHT, THEN GO TO THE BRITISH SECTOR UNTIL THINGS *COOLED OFF,* 

BUT EAST GERMAN COMMUNIST POLICE PICKED MIM UP AND TOOK HIM TO RUSSIAN 
INTELLIGENCE HEADQUARTERS ,

FACES A BRITISH ARMY TRIAL ON CHARGES OF DESERTION,

ALREADY CONSTITUTED *°CONSIDERABLE PUNISHMENT, 
THE PROSECUTION CHARGED SCHULTZ WAS A PREVIOUS OFFENDER AS AN 


ABSENTEE FROM DUTY °IN THIS HIGHLY IMPORTANT OUTPOST OF BERLIN,*® 


IN BATAVIA, N.Y,, SCHULTZ*S MOTHER, MRS, ERNEST F, SCHULTZ,

HE MIGHT GET TWO OR THREE YEARS,

SECCURES AGAINST THE FREE FLOW OF WORLD NEWS INCREASED 
IN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS OF THIS YEAR BUT THERE WERE SOME HEARTENING 
VICTORIES BY ALERT NEWSMEN AND MILITANT EDITORS OVER THE FOES OF A 

THIS IS DISCLOSED IN A SURVEY OF CENSORSHIP AND OTHER CONDITIONS 
HAMPERING THE FLOW OF NEWS. EVERY SIX MONTHS THE ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ASKS ITS CORRESPONDENTS IN ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD TO REPORT ON 
CONDITIONS. THE LATEST SURVEY, COVERING THE PERIOD SINCE JAN.1, 

HAS JUST BEEN COMPLETED. 

THE SOVIET UNION AND COMMUNIST CHINA, AND THE NATIONS THAT FOLLOW 
MOSCOW IN BLIND OBEDIENCE, CHOKE OFF AS TIGHT AS EVER THE FLOW 
OF NEWS FROM GREAT AREAS OF THE WORLD. IN LIEU OF NEWS COMES 
A CONSTANT BARRAGE OF PROPAGANDA, MUCII OF IT DISTORTING OF TRUTH. 

BUT THIS IS A CHALLENGE TO ALERT NEWSMEN, WHO PATIENTLY SIFT 
THROUGH THOUSANDS OF WORDS TO FIND CLUES AS’TO WHAT IS REALLY GOING oN. 
IN THE WORDS OF AP CORRESPONDENT FRED HAMPSON, CHIEF OF THE AP 
BUREAU AT HONG KONG, ON THE BORDER OF RED CHINA: 

*AFTER SCANNING A COUPLE OF HUNDRED PAGES OF STUFF ON SOME NEW 
NATIONAL PATRIOTIC MOVEMENT THE MEANING OF IT GRADUALLY DRAWS INTO 
FOCUS AND YOU CAN REALLY GET PRETTY CLOSE TO THE TRUTH. 

"BUT YOU MUST READ EVERYTHING BECAUSE PROPAGANDA BY ITS NATURE 
PUTS THE FACTS BETWEEN THE LINES OR OTHERWISE SOFTENS THE” AND YOU 
NEVER KNOW WHERE YOU WILL FIND THEM=-SOMETIMES RIGHT IN THE MIDDLE OF A 
MESS OF INANE DRIVEL ABOUT GERM WARFARE A TREMENDOUSLY REVEALING 
DISCLOSURE ABOUT INDUSTRIAL CONDITIONS IN MANCHURIA IS INADVERTENTLY 

THE AP CORRESPONDENT IN VIENNA, A LISTENING POST FOR WHAT GOES 
IN THE COMMUNIST SATELLITE NATIONS OF EUROPE, HAS A SIMILAR 
EXPERIENCE. AND THIS IS TRUE AT OTHER POINT? WHERE RUSSIAN 
NEWSPAPERS AND RADIO BROADCASTS ARE GIVEN CLOSE SCRUTINY BY MEN FAMILIAR 
WITH SOVIET AFFAIRS.

ARREST OF FOUR NEWSMEN FOR CRITIZING A CABINET MINISTER. THE MEN WERE 
RELEASED AND THE CABINET MINISTER RESIGNED.

WITHDRAW AN OFFENDING CLAUSE FROM A BILL AND SUBSTITUTE ONE WHICH 
ABSOLVED NEWSPAPERS FROM ANY LIABILITY IF THEY PRINTED FAIR AND 
ACCURATE REPORTS OF ANY PROCEEDINGS OF THE LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL.

KOREAN AIR ( 220) 

SEOUL, TUESDAY, JULY 1-(AP)-THE FIFTH AIR FORCE TODAY CLAIMED U.S. 
SABRE JETS HELD AN 18-TO-1 ADVANTAGE IN AERIAL COMBAT OVER NORTHWEST 
KOREA DURING JUNE, THE 24TH MONTH OF WAR. “ 

THE AIR FORCE SAID F-SS SABRES SHOT DOWN 18 RUSSIAN-MADE MIGS IN 
JUNE WHILE LOSING ONLY ONE SABRE IN AIR COMBAT. 

TOTAL COMMUNIST LOSSES DURING THE MONTH WERE 22 PLANES, WHILE TOTAL 
FIFTH AIR FORCE LOSSES BEHIND ENEMY LINES WERE 15. IN ADDITION TO Till 
18 MIGS DESTROYED BY SABRES, THE SWEPT-WING AMERICAN JETS DOWNED THREE 
PROPELLER DRIVEN RED FIGHTERS AND A MARINE NIGHT FIGHTER SHOT DOWN 
ANOTHER PROP=DRIVEN COMMUNIST PLANE. 

ALTHOUGH THE FIFTH AIR FORCE LOST ONLY ONE SABRE IN AIR COMBAT 
10 OTHER FIFTH AIR FORCE PLANES WERE SHOT DOWN BY COMMUNIST GROUND 
FIRE. FOUR PLANES FAILED TO RETURN FROM THEIR MISSION FOR UNKNOWN 
CAUSES. 

JOINT AIR FORCE=-NAVY-MARINE STRIKES ON RED POWER PLANTS, STARTING 
WITH THE 500 PLANE RAID ON JUNE 23, STOPPED PRODUCTION IN 13 NORTIf 
KOREAN HYDRO=ELECTRIC CENTERS, THE MONTHLY SUMMARY SAID. 

DURING JUNE, EMPIIASIS ON ATR ACTION WAS SWITCHED FROM BENIND-THE= 
LINES STRIKES TO CLOSE SUPPORT AS GROUND ACTION PICKED UP ALONG THE 
BATTLE FRONT. FIGHTER-BOMBERS AND LIGHT BOMBERS HARASSED ENEMY TROOPS 
DAY AND NIGHT AND INFLICTED MORE THAN 1,000 ENEMY CASUALTIES. 

BAD WEATHER DURING THE LAST THREE DAYS OF THE JUNE KEPT FIGHTER= 
BOMBERS ON THE GROUND. BUT B-26 ALL-WEATHER LIGHT BOMBERS WORMED 
STEADILY ON CLOSE AIR SUPPORT MISSIONS.

NIGHT LEAD RHEE 
BY WILLIAM JORDEN 

PUSAN, KOREA, TUESDAY, JULY 1-(AP)-PRESIDENT SYNGMAN.RHEE MAY 
TAKE HYS FEUD WITH THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY TO THE KOREAN PEOPLE BY A 
VOTE WHICH THE UNITED NATIONS WOULD BE ASKED TO OBSERVE, INFORMED 
SOURCES SAID TODAY. 

THE INFORMANTS REPORTED RHEE PLANNED TO ASK THE KOREANS To SAY BY 
SECRET BALLOT WHETHER THEY WANT HIM TO DISSOLVE THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY 
AND CALL AN ELECTION OF NEW ASSEMBLYMEN. 
oprgtits yCOULD NOT BE CONFIRMED AMONG INTIMATES OF THE 77-YEAR-OLD 

INFORMANTS SAID THE SECRET REFERENDUM WAS THE "DECISIVE MEASURE" 
WHICH RHEE TOLD THE ASSEMBLY IN A MESSAGE MONDAY HE PLANNED TO TAKE 
UNLESS THEY APPROVED HIS CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT FOR POPULAR ELECTION 
OF THE KOREAN PRESIDENT. THE ASSEMBLY NOW ELECTS THE PRESIDENT. 

IN HIS FEUD WITH THE ASSEMBLY, HE HAS DECLARED MARTIAL LAW. HIS 
POLICE HAVE ARRESTED ASSEMBLYMEN, SOME ON CHARGES OF BEING INVOLVED 
IN A COMMUNIST PLOT. ALLIED OBSERVERS DISCOUNT THE PLOT CHARGES. 

SUPPORTERS OF THE PRESIDENT SAID THAT IF HE DOFS PLAN A REFERENDUM 
IT WOULD SHOW HE WAS WILLING TO LET THE BALLOTS PROVE OR DISPROVE 
HIS ARGUMENTS. 

RHEE'S MESSAGE TO THE ASSEMBLY CALLED UPON THE MEMBERS TO ACCEPT 
HIS PROGRAM QUICKLY OR FACE THE PROSPECT OF DISSOLUTION. HE SAID IIE 


WOULD TAKE MEASURES "WITHIN A FEW DAYS" UNLESS IT ACTED.

LONDON, JUNE 30-(AP)“RED RIOTING ON_KQJE ISLAND WAS PART OF 
A DEEP-LATD PLOT TO SEIZE THE REAR-AREA ISLAND FOR THE COMMUNISTS, 
A GOVERNMENT WHITE PAPER SAID TONIGHT. 

THE PAPER, PUBLISHED ON THE EVE OF A PARLIAMENTARY DEBATE ON THE

JUNE 30-C€AP)“A SEATTLE ATTORNEY, GEORGE KAHIN, SAID TODAY 
HE PUR IASED THE TICKETS WHICH LED TO A FALSE REPORT THAT FAR EASTERN 
EXPERT OWEN LATIIMORE WAS PLANNING A TRIP TO RUSSIA. 

KAHIN MADE His STATEMENT TO REPORTERS AFTER HARRY A. JARVINEN 
TRAVEL AGENCY MANAGER, PLEADED INNOCENT IN FEDERAL COURT HERE TOBAY 
TO TWO COUNTS OF FURNISHING FALSE INFORMATION TO FEDERAL AGENTS, 

, JARVINEN, A FINNISH VETERAN OF THE RUSSO-FINNISH WAR, WAS INDICTED 
BY A FEDERAL GRAND JURY FRIDAY ON CHARGES HE FURNISHED FALSE INFORMA= 

CAHIN T HE HAD PURCHASED TICYETS FOR LATTIMORE. JOHNS 
HOPKINS UNIVERSITY SPECIALIST ON FAR EASTERN AFFAIRS. IN SEA 
AFTER LATTIMORE BECAME STRANDED BY AN AIRLINE N SEATTLE, 

BUT KAHIN SAID THE TICKETS WERE FOR RAIL PASSAGE TO BALTIMORE 
FROM SEATTLE AND NOT PLANE TICKETS TO RUSSIA, AS JARVINEN "TIPPED" 
AC. I. As AGENT HERE AT A DINNER PARTY. 

KAHIN SAID HE PURCHASED THE TICKETS AT JARVINEN'S AGENCY FOR 
LATTIMORE, WHO HAS DENIED HE PLANNED A TRIP BEHIND THE IRON CURTAIN, 
AFTER LATTIMORE LOOKED FO }IM-FOR AID-IN PURCHASING RAIL TICKETS, 
"SIMPLY BECAUSE HE KNEW MY SON,® 

KAHIN SAID HIS SON, WHO IS NOW AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR AT CORNELL 
UNIVERSITY, WAS AT THE TIME A MEMBER OF THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY 
FACULTY IN THE SAME DEPARTMENT AS LATTIMORE. THE TICKETS WERE 
PURCHASED AT JARVINEN'S AGENCY, KAHIN SAID, BECAUSE A GIRL IN HIS 
OFFICE KNEW SOMEONE AT THE TRAVEL AGENCY WHO COULD CET RAIL TICKETS, 
WHICH, AT THAT TIME, WERE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN. 

AFTER JARVINEN'S *TIP® TO THE Ce Ie A. AGENT, THE STATE DEPART@= 
MENT INSTRUCTED ALL PORTS OF ENTRY TO DENY LATTIMORE PERMISSION TO 
LEAVE THE COUNTRY. WHEN THE *TIP" PROVED FALSE. A FEDERAL GRAND JURY 
WAS CALLED INTO SESSION HERE AND RETURNED THE INDICTMENT AGAINST 
JARVINEN. THE STATE DEPARTMENT THEN APOLOGIZED TO LATTIMORE. 

THE COURT INDICATED THE CASE WOULD GO TO TRIAL PROBABLY IN 


SEPTEMBER.

NUCLEAR PHYSICISTS A ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION PERSONNEL HAS GIVEN

CTURE.

CHICACO SCIENTISTS WHO PLAYED A MAJOR PART IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE

UNITED NATIONS, NeY., JUNE 30-(AP)=THE CANADIAN DELEGATION 
TO THE UsNe CIRCULATED TODAY A STATEMENT BY THREE CANADIAN SCIENTISTS 
SAYING THAT NO SCIENTIFIC PROOF HAS BEEN GIVEN SO FAR TO SUPPORT 
COMMUNIST CHARGES THAT THE UeS. AND THE U.N. USED BACTERIAL WARFARE 


IN KOREA AND CHINA, 

THE ANALYSIS OF CHARGES BY SOVIET DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER JACOB A. 

MALIK AND DR. JAMES ENDICOTT, A FORMER MINISTER WHO IS CHAIRMAN OF THE 
CANADIAN PEACE CONGRESS 
MACDONALD COLLEGE, MCGILL UNIVERSITY; Ae We BAKER, HEAD OF THE DEPART- 
MENT OF ENTOMOLOGY AND ZOOLOGY, ONTARIO AGRICULTURAL COLLEGE; AND C. E. 
ATWOOD, ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF ZOOLOGY, UNIVERSITY OF TORONTO. 

CANADA IS A MEMBER OF THE UeN. DISARMAMENT COMMISSION. WHICH IS 
EXPECTED TO DEAL WITH THE PROBLEM OF CONTROLLING BACTERIAL WEAPONS. 

THE DOCUMENT WAS DISTRIBUTED BY THE DELEGATION AS THE U.S. DELEGATE 
TO THE SECURITY COUNCIL, ERNEST A. GROSS, MAPPED HIS STRATEGY FOR 
TOMORROW'S MEETING OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL (9230 AeM. EeSeTe) GROSS 
WILL DEMAND IMMEDIATE CONSIDERATION OF AN IMPARTIAL INVESTIGATION INTO 
THE COMMUNIST CHARGES. 

THE SCIENTISTS SAID MORE THAN 50,000 DISTINCT SPECIES OF INSECTS 
OCCUR IN KOREA AND NORTH CHINA. THEY QUOTED DR. ENDICOTT AS SAYING HE, 
HIMSELF, HAD CAUGHT SOME GERM-LADEN INSECTS AND THEY POINTED OUT THAT 
ANYONE COULD HAVE CAUGHT ANY NUMBER OF SPIDERS IN THE FIELDS IN 
CHINA AND KOREA AT THE TIME DR. ENDICOTT SAID HE GOT HIS INSECTS. 

THE SCIENTISTS SAID NONE OF THE EVIDENCE SUBMITTED BY THE COMMUNISTS 
TO BACK THEIR CHARGES COULD BE ACCEPTED AS SCIENTIFIC PROOF "SINCE IN 
NO CASES, APPARENTLY, WERE TESTS MADE OF INSECTS OR MATERIALS KNOWN 
TO BE OF LOCAL ORIGIN IN ORDER TO DETERMINE IF THEY CARRIED 
DISEASE GERMS.* 

"TO AN ENTOMOLOGIST,® THE STATEMENT SAID," IN ALL CASES WHERE 
IDENTIFICATION IS CERTAIN, THE INSECTS REFERRED TO ARE OBVIOUSLY CASUAL 
COLLECTIONS OF LOCAL FORMS."

ARRIVED, A GOOD SHOWING MEANS THE CLASS IS NEAR GRADUATION.

AND "JUST ABOUT TO FINISI! SCHOOL.®

NIGHT LEAD BUSINESS WOMEN 

BOSTON, JULY 1-(AP)-THE FOREIGN POLICY OF THE UNITED STATES MUST 
BE BASED ON REALITIES NOT ILLUSIONS, THE CHAIRMAN OF THE 
INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS COMMITTEE OF THE NATIONAL FEDERATION OF 
BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONAL WOMEN'S CLUBS SAID TODAY. 

MRS»*SUSANNA SHALLNA, BOSTON LAWYER, TOLD A WORKSHOP GROUP OF 
THE FEDERATION'S NATIONAL CONVENTIONS 

"WE ARE UNALTERABLY OPPOSED TO MISINFORMED PERSONS SEEKING TO 
UND RMINE, THE CONCEPT OF A PEACEFUL WORLD AS OUTLINED BY THE UNITED 

EVERY BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONAL WOMAN IN THIS TIME OF CRISIS MUST 
COMBAT MISINFORMATION WITH FACTS AND STRIVE FOR GREATER UNDERSTANDING 
OF THE IMPLICATIONS OF OUR TIME.” 

MRS.»SHALLNA SAID THE NATIONS QF THE WESTERN WORLD ARE VITAL TO 
THE FREE VORLD COMMUNITY, "IF IT IS TO PROSPER, IF IT IS EVEN TO 

"THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION,” SHE SAID, “DEPENDS NOT 
ONLY UPON THE ABILITY OF WESTERN EUROPE TO CARRY A FALR_SHARE OF THE

S7TH, FORMERLY AN OHIO NATIONAL GUARD DIVISION, WOULD BE DRAWN ON THIS

AND IN OTHER FOREIGN POSTS.

SITUATIONS WHICH MIGHT OTHERWISE HAVE TORN THE FREE WORLD APART AND 
PAVED THE WAY FOR COMMUNIST EXPANSION. IN INDONESIA. PALESTINE. AND 
KASHMIR THE UNITED NATIONS STOPPED SERIOUS FIGHTING AND PERSUADED 
THE COMBATANTS TO TAKE STEPS TOWARD A PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT OF THEIR 
DIFFERENCES. IN MANY OTHER CASES THE UNITED NATIONS HAS PREVENTED 
DISPUTES FROM ERUPTING INTO VIOLENCE. 

WE MUST REMEMBER THAT THE CHALLENGE OF INTERNATIONAL LAWLESSNESS 
IS NOT ONLY MILITARY BUT ALSO POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC. THE UNITED 
NATIONS IS HELPING DEPENDENT PEOPLES TO MOVE TOWARD GREATER FREEDOM. 
THE UNITED NATIONS IS TAKING MEASURES TO PROMOTE EXTENSIVE INTERNA- 
TIONAL PROGRESS IN SUCH FIELDS AS AGRICULTURE, COMMUNICATION AND 
TRANSPORTATION, EDUCATION, HEALTH, AND LIVING STANDARDS. ITS TECH- 
NICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS’ AND OUR’OWN POINT FOUR ACTIVITIES ARE 
PROVIDING DRAMATIC EXAMPLES OF TANGIBLE ACCOMPLISHMENTS AT RELATIVELY 
LITTLE COST. THE UNITED NATIONS IN THIS WAY IS HELPING TO BUILD 
HEALTHEIR SOCIETIES, WHICH IN THE LONG RUN ARE THE “EST DEFENSE AGAINST 
COMMUNISM AND THE BEST GUARANTY OF PEACE. 

DURING THE PAST SEVEN YEARS OUR WORK IN THE UNITED NATIONS HAS 
BEEN CARRIED OUT ON A STRICTLY NONPARTISAN BASIS. ABLE MEN AND 
WOMEN FROM BOTH POLITICAL PARTIES AND BOTH HOUSES OF CONGRESS HAVE 
REPRESENTED THIS COUNTRY IN THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY. NEVERTHELESS 
PARTISAN ATTACKS HAVE BEEN MADE ON THE UNITED NATIONS. SOME OF 
THESE ATTACKS ARE MADE IN A SPIRIT OF IMPATIENCE THAT CAN ONLY LEAD 
TO THE HOLOCAUST OF WORLD-YIDE WAR. MOST OF THOSE WHO URGE US 
TO "GO IT ALONE" ARE BLIND TO THE FACT THAT SUCK A COURSE WOULD 
DESTROY THE SOLID PROGRESS TOWARD WORLD PEACE WHICH THE UNITED NATIONS 
HAS MADE IN THE PAST SEVEN YEARS. I AM CONFIDENT THAT THE AMERICAN 
PEOPLE WILL REJECT THESE VOICES OF DESPAIR. WE CAN WIN PEACE. BUT 
WE CANNOT WIN IT ALONE. AND, ABOVE ALL, WE CANNOT WIN IT BY FORCE 
ALONE. WE CAN WIN THE PEACE ONLY BY CORTINUING TO WORK FOR INTER- 
NATIONAL JUSTICE AND MORALITY THROUGH THE UNITED NATIONS. (END TEXT)

BY NUNGAN, KOREA, WEDNESDAY, JULY 9-(AP)-KOREAN TRUCE NEGOTIATORS MET 
IN SECRET SESSION FOR THE SIXTH CONSECUTIVE DAY TODAY WITHOUT GIVING 
HINT WHETHER PROGRESS WAS MADE TOWARD BREAKING THE LONG STANDING 
DEADLOCK ON EXCHANGE OF WAR PRISONERS. 
IT WAS THE LAST MEETING OF ONE FULL YEAR OF TALKS.

» THE TWO SIDES AGREED TO MEET AGAIN TOMORROW.

WILLINGNESS" TO REACH AGREEMENT. )

IF ANY. HE CHARACTERIZED THE TALKS AS STILL BUSINESS-LIKE.

SECOND NJGHT LEAD WAR (220) (NO PICKUP) 
BY STAN CARTER 

S KOREA, WEDNESDAY, JULY 9-(AP)-TWO REINFORCEC CHINESE 

COMP IN HAND-TO-HAND FIGHTING TODAY DROVE ALLIED INFANTRYMEN OFF 
A NEWLY-WON HILL ON THE EAST-CENTRAL KOREAN BATTLEFRONT. 

GEN. MARK CLARK'S HEADQUARTERS COMMUNIQUE ANNOUNCED THE SCENE oF 
MAJOR GROUND FIGHTING SHIFTED FROM THE WESTERN TO THE CENTRAL SECTOR 
OF THE BATTLELINE. 

THE 350 TO 400 REDS SWARMED UP THE HILL IN THE PUKHAN RIVER VALLEY 
ON THE HEELS OF A SHATTERING ARTILLERY AND MORTAR BARRAGE FOR A BRIEF 
BUT SAVAGE ACTION, THE U.S. EIGHTH ARMY SAID. RED GUNNERS HURLED 
MORE THAN 84000 ROUNDS OF MORTAR AND ARTILLERY FIRE AT U.N. CENTRAL 

B-26 LIGHT BOMBERS STRUCK AT THREE IMPORTANT COMMUNIST SUPPLY 
CENTERS TUESDAY NIGHT AND EARLY WEDNESDAY. HIGH EXPLOSIVES WERE 
DROPPED ON YANGDOK, SEPORI AND ICHON, THE AIR FORCE SAID, WHILE OTHER 
BOMBERS ATTACKED COMMUNIST FRONTLINE POSITIONS. 

AIR FORCE THUNDERJETS UNLOADED MORE BOMBS ON THE BIG NUMBER TWO 
POWER PLANT AT CHANGJIN (CHOSEN) AFTER RECONNAISSANCE DISCLOSED THAT 
THE REDS WERE TRYING TO GET THE GENERATORS BACK IN OPERATION, THE 

THE PLANT WAS ONE OF 13 NORTH KOREAN HYDRO ELECTRIC STATIONS 
KNOCKED OUT IN BIG RAIDS TWO WEEKS AGO. 

HEAVY FIGHTING FIRST FLARED ON THE CENTRAL FRONT MONDAY NIGHT. 
ALLIED INFANTRYMEN KNOCKED OFF THE PUKHAN VALLEY HILL HAD CAPTURED 
THE HEIGHT TUESDAY. THEY HAD BEATEN BACK REPEATED RED COUNTERATTACKS, 

THE U.N. TROOPS PULLED BACK TO POSITIONS OCCUPIED BEFORE THE 
ENCOUNTER, THE ARMY SAID.

WASHINGTON JULY $=(AP)-ELEVEN GOVERNMENT AGENCIES REPORTEDLY 
RECOMMENDED TODAY TRE UNITED STATES CONTINUE MILITARY AND ECONOMIC 
AID TO DENMARK EVEN THOUGH THE DANES HAVE SOLD A 13,000-TON TANKER 
0 
INFORMED OFFICIALS SAID MUTUAL SECURITY DIRECTOR AVERELL HARRIMAN 
WILL MAKE HIS OWN RECOMMENDATION TO PRESIDENT TRUMAN, PROBABLY TO=- 


RROW. 
- THE UNITED STATES IS CONSIDERING WHETHER TO CUT OFF MILITARY AND 
ECONOMIC ASSISTANCE TO DENMARK BECAUSE THE SALE OF THE TANKER APPARENT- 
LY VIOLATED FOREIGN AID LEGISLATION. THIS CALLS ON PRESIDENT TRUMAN 
TO TERMINATE FOREIGN AID TO ANY COUNTRY WHICH KNOWINGLY PERMITS SHIP- 
MENTS OF STRATEGIC ITEMS TO COMMUNIST BLOC COUNTRIES. 

NO OFFICIAL WORD OF THE RECOMMENDATION BY THE AGENCIES WAS DIS- 
CLOSED. BUT OFFICIALS INDICATED BROADLY THAT ALL AGENCIES AGREED THAT 
IT WOULD HURT AMERICAN SECURITY SERIOUSLY IF THE UNITED STATES CUT OFF 
AID TO DENMARK OVER THE TANKER INCIDENT

TOOK INTO CONSIDERATION THAT DENMARK CONTRACTED TO BUILD THE TANKER IN 
1948 BEFORE PRESENT ARGOES ON SUCH SHIPMENTS WENT INTO EFFECT.

RIDGWAY DIRECT CONTROL OF ALL U.S. FORCES IN NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY 
ORGANIZATION AREAS OF EUROPE IN ADDITION TO HIS OVERALL AUTHORITY AS 
SUPREME COMMANDER OF THE WESTERN ALLIES

WILL BE KNOWN AS "COMMANDER IN CHIEF, U.S., EUROPEAN COMMAND, | 

DEFENSE OFFICIALS EXPLAINED THAT THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THE MODIFI&lt;- 
CATION OF COMMAND STRUCTURE WAS TO TIE UP LOOSE ENDS, PARTICULARLY IN 
THE FIELDS OF CONSTRUCTION AND SUPPLY. 

RIDGWAY"’S NEW RESPONSIBILITY, THE PENTAGON EXPLAINED, WILL EMBRACE 
ALL AMERICAN FORCES IN THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY AREAS IN ADDITION TO 
THOSE IN WESTERN GERMANY. U.S. FORCES IN BERLIN, AUSTRIA AND TRIESTE 
WILL REMAIN OUTSIDE OF THE NEW COMMAND.

SUPREME ALLIED COMMANDER IN EUROPE, AND HIS SUCCESSOR, GEN.RIDGWAY, BOTH 
HAD OPERATIONAL CONTROL OF ALL U.S. FORCES IN THESE AREAS, BUT ONLY 
IN THE EVENT OF AN EMERGENCY.

ARMY FORCES IN EUROPE, WILL BECOME DEPUTY COMMANDER IN CHIEF OF THE 

UNIFIED AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS UNDER RIDGWAY. HANDY WILL LEAVE HIS 

PRESENT HEADQUARTERS AT HEIDELBERG GERMANY, TO SET UP THE NEW DEPUTY 

COMMAND AT A HEADQUARTERS CLOSE TO’ THAT OF GENERAL RIDGWAY NEAR PARIS.

NIGHT LEAD DEFENSE FUNDS 

WASHINGTON, JULY 10=(AP)=A BILL PROVIDING $45,500 | 
DEFENSE FUNDS FOR THE NEXT 12 MONTHS WAS SIGNED SY PRESIfENT TRUMAN 
TODAY. 

IT FURNISHES THE CASH TO ESTABLISH A POWERFUL 143-WING AIR FORCE 


909,990 ¢B) IN 


BY THE MIDDLE OF 1955, 

THE EFFECTIVE STRENGTH OF THE AIR FORCE NOW IS ABOUT 
WING RANGES FROM ABOUT 12 HEAVY DOLIBERS TO 75 FIGHTERS, 
TRATIVE AND MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL. 

ALTHOUGH THE BILL GIVES THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE FIVE BILLION 
DOLLARS LESS THAN THE PRESIDENT REQUESTED, IT DOES NOT CARRY THE 45 
BILLION CEILING ON MILITARY SPENDING VOTES BY THE HOUSE. 

MILITARY LEADERS CONTEMPLATE SPENDING MORE THAN 50 BILLION THIS 
YEAR, DRAWING ON FUNDS PREVIOUSLY APPROPRIATED BY CONGRESS BUT NOT 
USED. THEY ARGUED THAT AN ARBITRARY CEILING WOULD WRECX THE MILITARY 
BUILDUP. THE CEILING WAS REMOVED WHEN SENATE AND HOUSE CONFEREES 
WORKED OUT A COMPROMISE BILL. _ 

THE BILL ALSO GIVES $45 A MONTH EXTRA IN COMBAT PAY FOR SERVICENEN 
IN KOREA SINCE THE FIGHTING BEGAN THERE. A MINIMUM OF SIX DAYS IN THE 
COMBAT AREA IS REQUIRED FOR EACH MONTH'S ELIGIBILITY. 

THE NAVY IS AUTHORIZED IN THE MEASURE TO BUILD A SECOND 55,990-TON 
AIRCRAFT CARRIER OF THE FORRESTAL CLASS. NO NEW FUNDS ARE SUPPLIED 
FOR THIS PROJECT, HOWEVER. ee 

UNDER THE BILL, THE ARMY GETS $12, 239,900,900 ¢B), THE NAVY $12,- 
842,000,000 AND THE AIR FORCE $21,112,004,904, 

(HEN CONGRESS TACKLED THE BILL ORIGINALLY, IT WAS BENT UPON CUTTING 
ALL THE BUDGET REQUESTS SHARPLY. THE HOUSE GHOPPED 560 MILLION FROI1 
THE AIR REQUESTS AND RECOMMENDED THAT THE AIR PROGRAM BE STRETCHED 
OUT INTO LATER YEARS. 

BUT MILITARY AND ADMINISTRATION LEADERS SUCCEEDED IN HAVING THE

PITISBURGH, JULY 10-(AP)-STEVE Ny FORMER CHAIRMAN 

OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY IN WESTERN PENNSYLVANIA, WAS SENTENCED 


TO 20 YEARS IN JAIL TODAY FOR SEDITYONs 

JUDGE HARRY Me MONTGOMERY, WHO PRESIDED AT NELSON'S TRIAL, 

ALSO FINED HIM $10,000 AND ORDERED HIM TO PAY COURT COSTS. 

IT WAS THE MAXIMUM PENALTY--AND THE STIFFEST SENTENCE EVER 
GIVEN A COMMUNIST IN PENNSYLVANIA. 

A JURY IN FEBRUARY CONVICTED NELSON OF VIOLATING THE STATE'S 
ANTI-SEDITION LAWe THAT ACT FORBIDS ADVOCATING MEASURES AIMED AT 
THE FORCIBLE OVERTHROW OF THE GOVERNMENT. 

NELSON ALSO FACES A FEDERAL SEDITION CHARGE FOR HIS ACTIVITIES 
IN WESTERN PENNSYLVANIA. 

IN ADDITION THE HOUSE UN-AMERICAN ACTIVITIES COMMITTEE IN 1948 
ACCUSED NELSON OF PASSING ATOMIC SECRETS HE OBTAINED FROM AN AMERICAN 
SCIENTIST TO THE RUSSIAN VICE CONSUL IN SAN FRANCISCO. NELSON AND THF 
SCIENTIST, PROF. JOSEPH We WEINBERG, HAVE DENIED THE CHARGE. 

WEINBERG WAS INDICTED IN MAY ON A CHARGE OF LYING UNDER OATH 
WHEN HE TOLD THE COMMITTEE THREE YEARS AGO HE WAS NEVER A MEMBER OF 
THE COMMUNIST PARTY. 

BEFORE IMPOSING SENTENCE, JUDGE MONTGOMERY TURNED DOWN A PLEA 
FOR MERCY AND LENIENCY REMARKING NELSON PREVIOUSLY WAS 
"ARROGANT AND DEFIANT." 

"HE EITHER IS INNOCENT AND DESERVES HIS FREEDOM OR HE IS 
GUILTY AND SHOULD BE GIVEN THE EXTREME PENALTY. THE JURY FOUND 


AS HE WAS LED FROM THE COURTROOM NELSON MUTTERED: 
"THIS IS AN INJUSTICE." 
HIS ATTORNEY, VICTOR RABINOWITZ OF NEW YORK, DECLARED: 
SPEECHES NOW BEING MADE AT THE REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ADVOCATE 
A CYANGE IN OUR GOVERNMENT. THAT'S ALL STEVE NELSON DID." 
N DEMANDING THE MAXIMUM PENALTY, SPECIAL ASSISTANT DISTRICT 
TTORNEY WILLIAM Fe CERCONE SAID3 
"THIS MAN IS A DANGER TO THE NATION. HE HAS TAKEN ADVANTAGE 
OF EVERY FREEDOM OF OUR COUNTRY WHICH HE TRIED TO DESTROY. HE 


wns SSRaED IN MOSCOW TO COME BACK TO AMERICA AND SABOTAGE OUR COUNTRY."

THE WESTERN ALLIES AGREED TO MEET WITH RUSSIA=-POSSIBLY ON A 
LOWER DIPLOMATIC LEVEL--FOR THE SPECIFIC PURPOSE OF CREATING AN 
IMPARTIAL COMMISSION TO DETERMINE WHETHER FREE ELECTIONS CAN BE HELD 
THROUGHOUT DIVIDED GERMANY. 

THEY ALSO GAVE MOTICE THE RUSSIANS MUST AGREE IN ADVANCE TO 
GENUINELY FREE ELECTIONS IN THE SOVIET ZONE AND TO PARTICIPATION OF 
A FREE GERMAN GOVERNMENT IN THE NEGOTIATION FOR A FINAL PEACE 


TREATY | 
HE WESTERN PROPOSAL, IN EFFECT, REJECTED THE RUSSIAN STAND THAT 
ONLY REPRESENTATIVES OF THE FOUR POWERS OCCUPYING GERMANY WERE 
QUALIFIED TO SUPERVISE ALL=CERMAN ELECTIONS. 
THE WEST WANTS THE PROPOSED ELECTION COMMISSION TO BE FREE TO GO 
ANYWHERE IN GERMANY WITHOUT SUPERVISION AND DEMANDS THAT THE 
COMMISSION'S RECOMMENDATIONS NOT BE SUBJECT TO VETO BY ANY OF THE 


OWERS 
aoa es OF THESE STIPULATIONS ARE GOING TO PLEASE THE RUSSIANS. 


NON 
MAY, INDEED, AGREE TO AN IMPARTIAL COMMISSION, BUT THEIR IDEA 
THEY MPARTIALITY is HARDLY LIKELY TO COINCIDE WITH THE WEST'S. 


THEY ARE ALMOST CERTAIN TO STICK TO THEIR LONG-STANDING SUPPORT OF 
THE VETO ON IMPORTANT DECISIONS. AND THEY WOUUB)BARDLY WANT THE 
COMMISSION TO GO ANYWHERE IT WANTS WITHOUT SOME KIND OF CHECK, 
CONTENDING THAT THIS WOULD OFFER AN EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITY FOR 


STERN INTELLIGENCE OPERATIONS.
